summary: Martin Haug studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn, learning under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Bonn, Heidelberg, Deccan College (1859–1866), and the University of Munich (from 1868).
Philosopher Martin Heidegger studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert and Edmund Husserl. He taught at Freiburg (1915–1923, 1928–1958) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Marburg and Freiburg under Eva Tichy, Helmut Rix, and others, later serving at Freiburg (~1999–2008) and Jena (from 2013).

Martin King Whyte is a scholar of Sinology who studied at Cornell and Harvard. He held academic posts at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University, and Harvard University (from 2000).

Martin Lehnert works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Freiburg and served as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich (attested 2016).
Martin Lowenthal works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu, and held posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen, Berlin, Heidelberg, and Munich. He taught at Munich, the University of Chicago (1990–2011), and the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (2013).
Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel and held a post there, attested in 2004.
Martin T. Adam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and McGill University, completing his PhD under Richard P. Hayes.

Martin Willson worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Yeshe Thubten, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under MA supervisor Lambert Schmithausen, earned her doctorate from the University of Vienna (attested 2012), and held a post there.

Martino Dibeltulo works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Michigan, completing his PhD under the supervision of Donald S. Lopez, Jr., and was mentored by Ester Bianchi (attested 2015).

Marvin Eisenberg worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Princeton University, and held a post at the University of Michigan from approximately 1949 to 1993.

Mary C. Wright was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Vassar College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University, later holding posts at Stanford University (1947) and Yale University (1959).

Mary Clabaugh Wright worked in Sinology and history. She studied at Vassar and Radcliffe (PhD 1951), served as curator at the Hoover Institution (1946–1959), and held a professorship at Yale University from 1959.
Mary Evelyn Tucker works in religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. She earned her PhD from Columbia, and held posts at Bucknell (~1989–2005), UC Berkeley, Harvard, and Yale (from ~2006).

Mary Haas was a linguist who studied at Earlham College, the University of Chicago, and Yale University under Edward Sapir. She held a post at the University of California, Berkeley, from approximately 1947 to 1977.
Mary Jaksch works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Peter Harvey at the University of Sunderland (attested 2007) and under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Mary Shepherd Slusser worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at Michigan, Columbia (PhD), NYU, and Harvard. She held posts at the U.S. Department of State, the National Museum of African Art, and the National Museum of Asian Art.
Marybeth White works in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed an honors degree at York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).
